messages:
Sam: quick q about 429 behavior when we do backfill/grace-window adjustments — is the intended client fallback: headers -> body -> assume soft-429?
Elena: short answer: headers first. body is advisory for clients that can’t read headers (old SDKs). soft-429? only if both missing.
Ajay: can we be explicit in the contract about a new header? e.g. `X-Quota-Grace-Window: 30s` meaning server may accept retries within that time without charging quota.
Maria: ^ yes please. our mobile SDK already wants a deterministic order. otherwise it retries too aggressively and burns bursts.
Ryan: question: when backfill runs (billing/reconciliation) and adds tokens retroactively, will we ever send a 200 for a previously-429ed request? or only allow replay from client?
Elena: we never mutate past responses. backfill only affects future admission. we may, however, change `X-Quota-Remaining` on the next request.
Sam: okay, so clients shouldn't expect idempotent recovery by server. good to call that out.
Ajay: one more: how should per-route buckets interact with global bursts? current implementation is layered: check per-route first, then global. should the header reflect both?
Maria: propose `X-Quota-Remaining-Route` + `X-Quota-Remaining-Account`. keeps it explicit.
Ryan: can we provide an example 429 body for SDKs? small and stable.
Elena: suggested body: `{"error":"quota_exceeded","retry_after":3,"hints":{"route_remaining":0,"account_remaining":120}}` — stable keys, clients parse `retry_after` then optionally look at hints.
Sam: adding to that: include `grace_window_seconds` in hints if active.
CI-bot: deploy-check: rate-limit-headers spec updated in branch `rl/headers-grace`; unit tests + schema lint passed.
Maria: awesome. Ajay, Ryan can you quick-review the branch? nothing blocking but want agreement on header names.
Ajay: will review in the next hour.
Ryan: skimming now, left a tiny comment re: header capitalization in the doc (we standardize on-`X-` all caps).
Sam: final ask: SDK teams — are we ok with fallback order documented as: 1) `X-Quota-Remaining*` headers, 2) `retry_after` in 429 body, 3) treat as soft-429 and exponential backoff if neither present?
Maria: yes, that's clear. SDKs will implement that.
Elena: I'll add a short paragraph to the contract doc and include the example header/body snippets.
Sam: thanks — dropping the snippets here for the doc: ```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
X-Quota-Remaining-Route: 0
X-Quota-Remaining-Account: 120
X-Quota-Grace-Window: 30
Content-Type: application/json

{"error":"quota_exceeded","retry_after":3,"hints":{"route_remaining":0,"account_remaining":120,"grace_window_seconds":30}}
```
Maria: perfect. I'll post a short note in the SDK weekly sync so mobile/web teams know to pick this up. :thumbsup:
Ajay: done reviewing — no objections, one nit about field name ordering. not a blocker.
Ryan: resolved my nit. Approving the branch.
Sam: leaving this thread — thanks folks, will merge once CI green and Ajay approves.
CI-bot: merge-check: all checks green, merge queued.
